Answer: C
Reason: The CT images demonstrate massive, diffuse dilation of the trachea and main bronchi (tracheobronchomegaly) with associated large intrapulmonary cystic spaces and diverticula, which are pathognomonic for Mounier-Kuhn syndrome. The "cavities" seen on X-ray correspond to these dilated airways and cysts, while the hilar opacity represents the markedly enlarged, fluid-filled central airways rather than a mass or lymphadenopathy.
